statements.text: Once again, we're seeing power and influence coming into this state and ruining things for us Mainers. We needed a pause on this because it takes our power. It takes our water. There's health effects. We need regulations because we don't know what they're doing without data, our information. We don't know all the health effects to our kids.
statements.venue: Campaign remarks on Mills' data center moratorium veto, quoted in Newsweek

statements.text: I am not the most knowledgeable person on AI, but I have tried to get up to speed. I don't know if we can stop it, but we need to make sure we are not paying more in electric rates because of data centers coming in. We need to make sure that our water rates are protected.
statements.venue: Town hall in Lewiston, via WMTW

statements.text:
Today I introduced my Agency Over AI Plan.

AI is going to revolutionize our economy and our culture. Maine must lead the way in ensuring Big Tech oligarchs don’t use this technology to destroy jobs, hijack our minds, worsen our isolation, and harm our children. https://t.co/PPkZsJJjei
Data centers cannot come into Maine and leave working people behind.

AI may be new, it certainly is new to a lot of us, but the political question is old. Who benefits, who pays and who decides? Under the Jackson administration I can assure you that tech billionaires will not be deciding this alone and not be getting their way.
statements.venue: Spectrum News, remarks releasing 'Agency over AI' plan (gubernatorial campaign)

statements.text:
We need to BAN Flock cameras in Maine.

You’ve probably noticed, but these little black cameras are appearing all over our state. They are AI-powered devices that steal our data without a warrant and distribute it to ICE agents and other federal agencies without our knowledge or permission. 

This bullshit should be illegal. Under a Jackson administration, it will be.

I want to make sure that we know what the data is. How they are using it, and there has to be real parameters, real guidelines to how we're going to do this. I'm not really supportive of data centers, but I understand they're maybe something that we have to deal with.
statements.venue: Maine Senate debate, quoted in Newsweek

statements.text: I am very much in favor of making sure the federal government or the state of Maine puts guardrails on these things because I don't want the billionaires, again, writing the rules and making our communities worse off than they are right now.
statements.venue: Maine Senate debate, quoted in Newsweek
